title: Finite split coefficient extension of a given monic relation
statement: Let $R$ be a normal Nagata domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] and $K$ its fraction field, both in universe $u$. For $x\in K$, put $S=R[x]$, and let $I$ be any ideal of $S$. Given a monic polynomial $f\in R[X]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] of positive degree with $f(x)\in I$, there exist a normal Nagata domain $R\prime$ with fraction field $K\prime$, both in universe $u$, $z\in K\prime$, an injective finite map $g:S\to R\prime[z]$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and a monic positive-degree polynomial $f\prime\in R\prime[X]$ which splits over $R\prime$ and whose evaluation at $z$ belongs to $I R\prime[z]$ along $g$. No maximality assumption on $I$ is needed.

proof.text: Let F=Frac(R), q the coefficient image of f, and L=q.SplittingField. Mathlib supplies a finite field extension and splitting of q. Put C=integralClosure R L. NagataDomainN2 supplies Module.Finite R C. Mathlib integral-closure finite-extension results make C normal with fraction field L; finite Nagata ascent makes C Nagata.

Map K into L through its fraction-field equivalence with F; let z be the image of x and restrict to an injective map g:S -> C[z]. The tensor map S tensor_R C -> C[z] is surjective: adjoin induction produces a preimage for z from x tensor 1 and for each coefficient from 1 tensor c. Module.Finite.base_change and of_surjective show g finite.

Set fprime=f.map (algebraMap R C). Every root of its image in L lies in C by roots_mem_integralClosure. Splits.of_splits_map_of_injective descends splitting. The injective coefficient map preserves monicity and degree. aeval_map_algebraMap and aeval_algHom_apply identify fprime(z) with g(f(x)), which is in I.map g by mem_map_of_mem.
